## What it is

<!-- KEEP:what-it-is:START -->
The generic, tenant-scoped audit log: `CORE_AUDIT_EVENT` (action, actor and realm, entity type and id, bilingual
summary, redacted `CHANGES` as JSON, ip, user agent, reference). Rows are written in-process only — by the
`@Audited` entity listener (one `CREATE` / `UPDATE` / `DELETE` row per change, same transaction, sensitive field
names redacted) and by `AuditApi.record(AuditEntry)` for business actions — read through
`POST /api/v1/audit/events/search` and the `AUDIT_EVENTS` report, and deleted only by retention
(`erp.core.audit.retention-days`, tenant by tenant through `TenantRunner`).
<!-- KEEP:what-it-is:END -->

## When to use it

<!-- KEEP:when-to-use:START -->
On every entity whose changes a reviewer may need to see: `@Audited(entityType = "<TABLE>", ignore = {…})`. For a
business action that is not a row change (approve, post, export, print): `AuditApi.record`. Not for the security
events of SEC (`SEC_AUDIT_LOG` is SEC's own) and not for application logging.
<!-- KEEP:when-to-use:END -->

## How to call it

<!-- KEEP:how-to-call:START -->
```java
// every insert, update and delete of the entity becomes one audit row (same transaction)
@Audited(entityType = "SHOP_ORDER", ignore = {"internalNote"})
public class Order extends AuditableEntity { … }

// a business action
auditApi.record(AuditEntry.builder()
    .action("APPROVE").entityType("SHOP_ORDER").entityId(order.getId().toString())
    .summaryAr("اعتماد الطلب " + order.getOrderNo()).summaryEn("Order " + order.getOrderNo() + " approved")
    .change(new AuditChange("status", "SUBMITTED", "APPROVED"))
    .build());
```
<!-- KEEP:how-to-call:END -->

## Do not rebuild

<!-- KEEP:do-not-rebuild:START -->
A history / changes / log table, a Hibernate envers-style listener, a "who changed what" column set beyond the
audit columns, a retention job of your own.
